docs.title: Diagnostic codes
docs.text:
Every compiler diagnostic carries a four-character prefix plus a four-digit number: GP for the parser / lexer, GR for name resolution, GT for the type checker, GM for match exhaustiveness, GL for lint framework, GK for the package manager. Use gos explain <code> for the interactive version. This page is auto-generated from the catalogue in xtask/src/main.rs; hand edits are overwritten by cargo xtask docs-diagnostics.

Code Phase Title GP0001 Parser unexpected token GP0002 Parser unexpected end of input GP0003 Parser unterminated delimiter GP0004 Parser chained comparison without parentheses GP0005 Parser chained range operator GP0006 Parser struct literal in scrutinee GP0007 Parser pipe right-hand side not callable GP0008 Parser assignment outside statement position GP0009 Parser expected integer literal GP0010 Parser expected string literal GP0011 Parser invalid tuple index GP0012 Parser malformed label GP0013 Parser malformed attribute GP0014 Parser malformed use declaration GP0015 Parser unexpected construct GP0016 Parser reserved extern keyword GR0001 Resolve unresolved name GR0002 Resolve wrong namespace GR0003 Resolve duplicate item GR0004 Resolve duplicate import GT0001 Types type mismatch GT0002 Types unresolved method GT0003 Types unresolved operator GT0004 Match exhaustiveness non-exhaustive match GT0005 Types non-primitive cast GK0001 Package manager manifest parse error

docs.title: GP0001
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected token

The parser saw a token where it expected a different one. Check for missing punctuation, an unmatched delimiter, or an out-of-place keyword.

docs.title: GP0002
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected end of input

The parser reached end-of-file in the middle of a construct. Finish the expression, statement, or item - or remove it.

docs.title: GP0003
docs.text:
Parser - unterminated delimiter

A balanced construct (block, tuple, array, string literal) was left unterminated. Add the matching closing delimiter.

docs.title: GP0004
docs.text:
Parser - chained comparison without parentheses

Comparison operators like == / != / < are not associative. Parenthesise the operands: (a == b) && (b == c).

docs.title: GP0005
docs.text:
Parser - chained range operator

Range operators (.., ..=) are not associative. Parenthesise the operands: (a..b)..c.

docs.title: GP0006
docs.text:
Parser - struct literal in scrutinee

A braced struct literal in the scrutinee of if/while/match is ambiguous with the block. Wrap the literal in (...).

docs.title: GP0007
docs.text:
Parser - pipe right-hand side not callable

The right-hand side of |> must be a callable: a function reference, a method call, or a closure.

docs.title: GP0008
docs.text:
Parser - assignment outside statement position

Assignment (=, +=, …) only appears at statement position. If you need an expression, return the right-hand side directly.

docs.title: GP0009
docs.text:
Parser - expected integer literal

An integer literal is required at this position.

docs.title: GP0010
docs.text:
Parser - expected string literal

A string literal is required at this position.

docs.title: GP0011
docs.text:
Parser - invalid tuple index

A tuple index must be a plain decimal integer (p.0, p.1). Hex, binary, or octal indices are not accepted.

docs.title: GP0012
docs.text:
Parser - malformed label

A label identifier is required after the leading '.

docs.title: GP0013
docs.text:
Parser - malformed attribute

An attribute is malformed. Accepted forms are #[attr], #[attr(args)], and #[attr = value].

docs.title: GP0014
docs.text:
Parser - malformed use declaration

A use declaration could not be parsed. Check the path for stray punctuation or an unfinished brace list.

docs.title: GP0015
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected construct

Two consecutive tokens formed something the parser does not recognise.

docs.title: GP0016
docs.text:
Parser - reserved extern keyword

The extern keyword is reserved but has no source-level item form. Gossamer's FFI surface is the [rust-bindings] section of project.toml plus the gossamer-binding crate.

docs.title: GR0001
docs.text:
Resolve - unresolved name

A name used in source could not be resolved to a declaration. Check the spelling, whether a use brings the name into scope, and whether the item is visible at this location.

docs.title: GR0002
docs.text:
Resolve - wrong namespace

A name was resolved to the wrong namespace (value vs. type). Check the declaration and the spelling.

docs.title: GR0003
docs.text:
Resolve - duplicate item

Two items in the same module share a name. Rename one of them or move it into a distinct mod.

docs.title: GR0004
docs.text:
Resolve - duplicate import

The same path was imported twice in the same use list. Drop the duplicate.

docs.title: GT0001
docs.text:
Types - type mismatch

The type checker could not reconcile two types it expected to match. The primary label shows the location of the mismatch; the note: line names the conflicting types.

docs.title: GT0002
docs.text:
Types - unresolved method

The type checker could not find a method with the supplied name on the receiver type. Check for a typo, a missing use, or a trait impl that lives in an unreachable module.

docs.title: GT0003
docs.text:
Types - unresolved operator

The operator is not defined for the operand types. Check the operand types and use the correct operator.

docs.title: GT0004
docs.text:
Match exhaustiveness - non-exhaustive match

A match expression does not cover every possible value. Add an arm for the pattern(s) listed under help:.

docs.title: GT0005
docs.text:
Types - non-primitive cast

The as cast is restricted to a whitelist: numeric ↔ numeric, bool/char → integer, u8 → char, and same-type no-ops. Struct / enum / String sources are rejected. Use a conversion method when you need serialisation; as does not run code.

docs.title: GK0001
docs.text:
Package manager - manifest parse error

The package manifest (gos.toml) could not be parsed. Check the TOML syntax and required fields.

docs.title: Lints
docs.text:
The Gossamer linter ships 50 day-one checks. Each has a short identifier suitable for #[lint(allow(...))] and a long-form explanation available via gos lint --explain <id>. This page is auto-generated from gossamer-lint; hand edits are overwritten on the next run of cargo xtask docs-lints.

Code Identifier Default GL0001 unused_variable warn GL0002 unused_import warn GL0003 unused_mut_variable warn GL0004 needless_return warn GL0005 needless_bool warn GL0006 comparison_to_bool_literal warn GL0007 single_match warn GL0008 shadowed_binding warn GL0009 unchecked_result warn GL0010 empty_block warn GL0011 panic_in_main warn GL0012 redundant_clone warn GL0013 double_negation warn GL0014 self_assignment warn GL0015 todo_macro warn GL0016 bool_literal_in_condition warn GL0017 let_and_return warn GL0018 collapsible_if warn GL0019 if_same_then_else warn GL0020 redundant_field_init warn GL0021 needless_else_after_return warn GL0022 self_compare warn GL0023 identity_op warn GL0024 unit_let warn GL0025 float_eq_zero warn GL0026 empty_else warn GL0027 match_bool warn GL0028 needless_parens warn GL0029 manual_not_equal warn GL0030 nested_ternary_if warn GL0031 absurd_range warn GL0032 string_literal_concat warn GL0033 chained_negation_literals warn GL0034 if_not_else warn GL0035 empty_string_concat warn GL0036 println_newline_only warn GL0037 match_same_arms warn GL0038 manual_swap warn GL0039 consecutive_assignment warn GL0040 large_unreadable_literal warn GL0041 redundant_closure warn GL0042 empty_if_body warn GL0043 bool_to_int_match warn GL0044 fn_returns_unit_explicit warn GL0045 let_with_unit_type warn GL0046 useless_default_only_match warn GL0047 unnecessary_parens_in_condition warn GL0048 pattern_matching_unit warn GL0049 panic_without_message warn GL0050 empty_loop warn

docs.title: unused_variable
docs.text: Declares a let binding whose name is never read. Prefix the name with _ to silence explicitly (e.g. _tmp) when the binding is intentional but unused.

docs.title: unused_import
docs.text: A use declaration whose imported name is never referenced. Remove the import or reference the name in the file.

docs.title: unused_mut_variable
docs.text: A binding marked mut that is never reassigned. Drop the mut keyword.

docs.title: needless_return
docs.text: return expr at the tail of a block is the same as writing expr by itself. Prefer the tail form for symmetry with the rest of the expression language.

docs.title: needless_bool
docs.text: if cond { true } else { false } is the same as cond. The inverted form is !cond.

docs.title: comparison_to_bool_literal
docs.text: x == true reads worse than x, and x == false reads worse than !x. Drop the literal.

docs.title: single_match
docs.text: A match with a single arm reads better as if let PATTERN = .... Single-arm match is almost always a half-written exhaustive match.

docs.title: shadowed_binding
docs.text: A let binding in the same block shadows an earlier one. Rename one of them to make the data flow obvious.

docs.title: unchecked_result
docs.text: let _ = expr? silently discards an error. Either handle the Err branch explicitly or propagate with ? so the caller sees it.

docs.title: empty_block
docs.text: An empty {} block is almost always a mistake. Add an explicit () tail if the block is intentional.

docs.title: panic_in_main
docs.text: panic! inside main aborts without a clean exit code. Return a Result from main and use ? so the error propagates.

docs.title: redundant_clone
docs.text: Calling .clone() on a literal or already-copied value is redundant. Drop the call.

docs.title: double_negation
docs.text: !!x collapses to x when x: bool. If the double negation is intentional for truthiness coercion, use an explicit cast.

docs.title: self_assignment
docs.text: Assigning a variable to itself does nothing. The statement is usually the residue of a refactor - remove it.

docs.title: todo_macro
docs.text: todo!() and unimplemented!() are placeholders, not shippable expressions. Implement the branch before merging.

docs.title: bool_literal_in_condition
docs.text: if true { ... } / while false { ... } - the branch is decided at compile time. Drop the control-flow construct.

docs.title: let_and_return
docs.text: let x = expr; x at the tail of a block is just expr. Drop the needless binding.

docs.title: collapsible_if
docs.text: if a { if b { ... } } can be combined into if a && b { ... }. Easier to scan.

docs.title: if_same_then_else
docs.text: Both branches of the if are identical. Drop the branch and keep the body once.

docs.title: redundant_field_init
docs.text: Foo { x: x } is the same as the shorthand Foo { x }.

docs.title: needless_else_after_return
docs.text: if cond { return X } else { Y } - the else is unreachable fall-through. Un-nest the else body.

docs.title: self_compare
docs.text: Comparing a value to itself is always true (for ==, <=, >=) or false (for !=, <, >). Use the constant.

docs.title: identity_op
docs.text: x + 0, x - 0, x * 1, x / 1 all equal x. The operation adds nothing but noise.

docs.title: unit_let
docs.text: let x = () binds the unit value, which is almost never useful. Drop the let.

docs.title: float_eq_zero
docs.text: Equality against a float literal is almost never what you want - floating-point arithmetic rarely produces the exact bit pattern. Compare (x - y).abs() < eps with an explicit tolerance.

docs.title: empty_else
docs.text: else {} adds no information. Drop the else and let the if stand alone.

docs.title: match_bool
docs.text: match b { true => ... false => ... } is an if in disguise. Rewrite as if b { ... } else { ... }.

docs.title: needless_parens
docs.text: (x) without a trailing comma is a needless pair of parens - x reads the same. (x,) is a one-tuple and means something different.

docs.title: manual_not_equal
docs.text: !(a == b) is just a != b. Prefer the direct operator.

docs.title: nested_ternary_if
docs.text: Three or more nested if / else if layers are hard to skim. Rewrite as match on the discriminant.

docs.title: absurd_range
docs.text: A literal range whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound is empty. Swap the bounds or double-check the intent.

docs.title: string_literal_concat
docs.text: "a" + "b" can be written directly as "ab". Let the source reflect the final value.

docs.title: chained_negation_literals
docs.text: -(-x) is x. The extra unary does nothing.

docs.title: if_not_else
docs.text: if !cond { A } else { B } scans better as if cond { B } else { A }. Flip the branches and drop the !.

docs.title: empty_string_concat
docs.text: Concatenating an empty string literal is a no-op. Drop the "" + or + "".

docs.title: println_newline_only
docs.text: println("") already writes a newline. Don't pass "\n" and don't call it twice to emit a blank line.

docs.title: match_same_arms
docs.text: Two match arms share the same body. Either collapse them with | alternation or extract the shared body into a helper.

docs.title: manual_swap
docs.text: Three consecutive statements let tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp swap two bindings via a temporary. Prefer a destructuring assignment once the language supports it, or at minimum document why the swap is needed.

docs.title: consecutive_assignment
docs.text: Two back-to-back assignments to the same place - the earlier value is dead before it's read. Drop the first or consolidate the logic into one statement.

docs.title: large_unreadable_literal
docs.text: Integer literals of five or more digits are easier to scan with _ as thousands separators: 1_000_000 instead of 1000000.

docs.title: redundant_closure
docs.text: |x| f(x) is a closure that just forwards to f. Pass f directly.

docs.title: empty_if_body
docs.text: An if cond { } else { body } is the same as if !cond { body }. Invert the condition and drop the empty branch.

docs.title: bool_to_int_match
docs.text: match b { true => 1, false => 0 } is an if in disguise that happens to return an integer. Prefer if b { 1 } else { 0 }.

docs.title: fn_returns_unit_explicit
docs.text: fn f() -> () { ... } is the same as fn f() { ... }. The explicit -> () is noise.

docs.title: let_with_unit_type
docs.text: let _: () = expr annotates the binding with the unit type. If expr was going to return () anyway, the annotation is noise. If it wasn't, the annotation forces a coercion - use a plain statement instead.

docs.title: useless_default_only_match
docs.text: match x { _ => expr } always runs expr - the match adds nothing. Drop the match (and add let _ = x if evaluating the scrutinee has side effects).

docs.title: unnecessary_parens_in_condition
docs.text: if (cond) { ... } wraps the condition in a single-tuple expression. Drop the parens: if cond { ... }.

docs.title: pattern_matching_unit
docs.text: match () { ... } has exactly one reachable arm. Drop the match and run the body directly.

docs.title: panic_without_message
docs.text: panic() with no argument leaves the post-mortem with nothing to render. Always pass a brief explanation.

docs.title: empty_loop
docs.text: loop {} with no body busy-waits forever at 100% CPU. Add a break, a continue, or replace with a real wait primitive.
